newsitem.title: USA: Flagstar says to file voluntary chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Flagstar says to file voluntary chapter 11.

text.p: Flagstar Corp said on Monday that it and certain holders of its 10 percent convertible junior subordinated debentures due 2014 have agreed to dismiss an involuntary Chapter 11 proceeding, so the company could file its own bankruptcy plan.
Flagstar said the agreement will allow the restaurant chain to continue the solicitation of votes for its financial restructuring.
Flagstar said the Chapter 11 will involve the parent company only, but will not involve its restaurant subsidiaries, which include Denny's, El Pollo Loco and Quincy's Family Steakhouse.
Ballots for the company's solicitation are due midnight on July 7, 1997, unless extended.

The financial restructuring would provide holders of the company's $847 million of senior subordinated debentures with 95.5 percent of the common equity of the reorganized company, the company had said on March 17 when the plan was proposed.
Convertible junior subordinated debtholders would get a 3.25 percent stake, Flagstar had said.

Preferred stockholders would receive 1.25 percent of the new company's equity, while common stockholders would get warrants to acquire seven percent of the recapitalized company on a fully diluted basis, Flagstar had said.
